A landing that changes athena.toml, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain.toml or docs/system-facts.md now triggers a rebuild. This is correct, because athena-gate BUILTIN_CONFIG and briefs SYSTEM_FACTS build those files in via include_str!. It is recorded in CHANGELOG and D158, and the drain tests were extended.

summary: The change fixes the shared cause at its source. One registry, `athena_core::mirrors::REGISTRY`, lists each file kept by hand as a copy of a governing source, and each entry has a rule that compares content, not just shape. Four rules: shard timings against the test files on disk, the decision log against its base text (append-only), the CI athena-bin cache key against BUILD_PATHS in both directions, and ontology lines in governing docs against each term's senses or excuses. The registry runs in two places. The producer loop runs it before verification and sends a drift back once. The new `athena-cli --test mirrors` target runs every entry over the real files, plus a broken fixture for each entry. The root cause is named in the same words in the mirrors.rs module doc, the CHANGELOG bullet and the new decision D158, which is purely appended. Making the CI key and BUILD_PATHS agree meant adding four paths to BUILD_PATHS, and that is correct: athena.toml, defaults.toml and docs/system-facts.md are built into the binary via `include_str!`, so the drain was missing rebuilds before. I ran four commands in this snapshot and all passed: `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors` (27 tests, including 7 producer-loop tests), `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors --test ontology` (4 and 30 tests), and the brief test. fmt, clippy and the full test suite come from Athena's CI record. Athena's revert runs show the new tests fail without the change: two fail to compile, and the brief test's assertion fails. The findings are minor: some changed files are outside the expected-deliverables list (all needed and almost all planned), checks.rs was listed but not changed (D158 explains why), and the repo-level append-only check compares against HEAD.
